blocks.h2: Why Sewer Lines Fail in Elmhurst
blocks.intro: The median Elmhurst home was built in 1966. About 4 in 10 went up between 1940 and 1969, and about 1 in 7 is older still.

items.body: Most lines from the 1940s to the 1960s are vitrified clay. The pipe itself lasts, but the joints let roots in.
Homes built before 1940 can have clay or cast iron that's been patched more than once.
Mature trees along Elmhurst's streets have had 60 years to find the sewer.
About 3 in 10 homes were built after 1990, some tied into older connections at the street.

blocks.h2: How We Repair a Sewer Line
blocks.intro: Once we know what's wrong, there's usually more than one way to fix it. Which method makes sense depends on the pipe's condition, location, and how it failed.
head: Method
What It Involves
Typical Disruption
rows: A resin-coated liner is pulled through the existing pipe and cured in place, creating a new pipe inside the old one.
Minimal digging, usually just small access points
A new pipe is pulled through the old one while a bursting head fractures the old pipe outward to make room.
Minimal digging, works even when the old pipe is badly damaged
The damaged section is dug up and replaced directly.
More digging, but sometimes the only option depending on damage location and access
blocks.note: In Elmhurst, the line often passes under a mature parkway tree and a front walk. The footage tells us which method keeps both.

blocks.body: About 3 in 10 Elmhurst homes were built in 1990 or later, many on lots where an older house came down. A new home doesn't always mean a new sewer line. Sometimes the builder connected to the original lateral to the street. If your newer home has root clogs or slow drains, a camera inspection will show whether part of the line is older clay that never got replaced.

blocks.h2: Sewer Repair Questions From Elmhurst Homeowners

items.q: Why does my sewer line keep needing cleaning?
items.preview: Usually roots coming through a damaged joint.
items.answer: Usually roots growing through a cracked or separated clay joint. Cleaning removes them, but they grow back until the joint is sealed or replaced.

items.q: Is a liner better than digging?
items.preview: Often, if the pipe still holds its shape.
items.answer: Often. A [trenchless liner](/elmhurst/trenchless-sewer-repair) seals every joint from inside without a trench. A collapsed or sagging section still needs a spot dig.

items.q: Who is responsible for the line under the parkway?
items.preview: Usually the homeowner, to the city main.
items.answer: In most cases, the homeowner is responsible for the line from the house to the city main. We'll show you where the problem is on camera.

items.q: Should I fix the sewer before finishing my basement?
items.answer: Yes. Scope the line and the under-floor drains first. It's much cheaper than opening a finished floor later.

items.q: Do I need a permit for sewer repair in Elmhurst?
items.answer: Usually. We handle the permit for the work we do.

items.q: How much does sewer line repair cost in Elmhurst?
items.preview: It depends on the damage and the method. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on what the camera finds, the depth, the repair method and what sits above the line. You'll approve a flat-rate price before any work.
